title: Mac self-host origin and transport correction — new candidate acceptance
scope: Explicitly authorized narrow origin/transport source correction, new clean candidate and private synthetic whole-image acceptance. No real-provider inference or production rollout.

root_cause.origin: Next 15.5.25 constructs the native request URL from the fixed internal listener, 0.0.0.0:3000. A request whose raw Host was nova.galx.ai reached authorization with https://0.0.0.0:3000/v1/inference. The old exact configured-resource comparison returned 401 before database admission, although direct repository admission for the same synthetic authority passed.
root_cause.callback: The NextURL accessor also applies unanchored loopback normalization to the serialized URL, changing an embedded registered redirect_uri from 127.0.0.1:4401 to localhost:4401. Exact callback validation correctly rejected this mutated query. Reading the original native URL preserves the registered callback without expanding trust.
fixture_corrections: Node fetch did not send the requested Host override; raw node:http is used for exact authority tests. No application bypass was added.

The existing endpoint policy correctly rejected plain HTTP on a Docker hostname. The final isolated provider fixture shares an anchored internal network namespace with the application and uses authenticated HTTP loopback. Provider authority remains outside browser/client state. No application endpoint policy change was made.

trust_model.internal_listener: 0.0.0.0:3000 inside the container; operator publication only at 127.0.0.1:17787 on the Mac
trust_model.configuration: The bootstrap exclusively selects GALX_REQUEST_ORIGIN_MODE=mac-loopback-v1 and GALX_SELF_HOST_AUTHORITY=0.0.0.0:3000. Incoming metadata, ambient overrides and private JSON cannot choose this trust mode.
trust_model.resolution: Require the native fixed listener, then select only exact HTTPS authorities from NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, GALX_CONNECT_ORIGIN and GALX_NOVA_RESOURCE. Raw Host is a bounded virtual-host selector, not an identity credential. Unknown hosts, ports and raw loopback aliases fail closed. Canonical scheme is configured, not forwarded.
trust_model.untrusted_metadata: Origin, Forwarded, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto and forwarded ports cannot select canonical identity. Browser Origin is independently checked by the existing registered-client/same-origin policy.
trust_model.direct_deployment: Default direct mode retains native Request authority and exact IP-loopback ports. Forged header claims cannot rewrite it.
trust_model.authorization: Issuer, Nova audience, inference scope, client registration, PKCE, current application grant and explicit entitlement remain independently mandatory. Canonical Host, loopback reachability and a GALX browser cookie confer no Nova authority.
trust_model.callback: Original native query parameters and validated registered redirect are preserved exactly. Account/workspace redirects and cookie mutation checks share the helper.
trust_model.future_ingress: No public proxy trust relationship is established. Public routing needs separately reviewed exact host/path ingress, private-surface denial and acceptance.

source_correction.transport: Pull-based 15-second SSE comment keepalive, one pending upstream read/timer, private/no-store/no-transform; one SSE invocation with bounded terminal-validated default JSON aggregation in the first-party SDK.

source_correction.unchanged: Dependency lock; GALX identity; grant/entitlement storage; PKCE; audience/scope; revocation; quota arithmetic; provider-health classification; admission; terminal state machine; duplicate/no-replay; existing routing strategy; pricing/Media.

incremental_chromium.scope: Test-only loopback ingress forwards once to the packaged image; hash-verified candidate client buffer; no deployed proxy.

transport.cancellation: After stream initiation, client abort propagated; execution persisted unknown; no automatic replay.
transport.disconnect: Lost client socket persisted unknown, no added explicit provider-failure signal, no replay.
transport.deadline: Unchanged 300-second execution deadline with SIGTERM during the active request: unknown persisted, 304278 ms total, 19 heartbeats, clean exit 0, no added provider-failure signal.
transport.duplicate: 409 refers to the existing execution; provider-attempt count remains unchanged. This is the existing retained-execution contract, not a new stream-resume feature.
transport.replay_protection: SDK submits exactly once; fixed fixture ingress forwards once; Nova retains duplicate admission and unknown/no-replay behavior. No new production proxy/retry layer introduced. Future public ingress is outside this acceptance.
transport.provider_failure: Controlled explicit failure contributes one fixture failure signal; provider drops/incomplete output/cancellation/deadline do not. Actual relay provider-health behavior is independently covered by the 98 established checks; no health implementation changed.
transport.capacity: Two concurrent admitted requests; excess request rejected 503 without provider dispatch. Grant permission does not bypass available capacity.

whole_image_acceptance.database: Disposable PostgreSQL 17/pgvector; 159-migration chain; no production database mutation.
whole_image_acceptance.authorization_path: Actual packaged HTTP authorize, PKCE exchange, refresh and revoke; synthetic account session/consent actor directly decides consent through the repository. No real portal sign-in is claimed.
whole_image_acceptance.archive: Retained archive SHA verified and reloaded via docker load; immutable image ID and manifest labels checked.
whole_image_acceptance.runtime_policy: Loopback only, non-root, read-only, bounded memory/CPU/PIDs/cache/logs, immutable image, private file configuration, 480-second shutdown grace.
whole_image_acceptance.restart: Graceful stop/start reseeds only disposable cache; unknown/completed execution records and revoked grants remain unchanged; duplicate dispatch denied.
whole_image_acceptance.hard_crash: SIGKILL cannot commit a terminal write. The original running row remains retained; public duplicate outcome is unknown and restart does not dispatch again. One automatic container restart observed; no historical execution mutation.
limits: Synthetic account session/consent actor and provider; actual packaged HTTP authorization initiation, PKCE exchange, refresh, revocation and inference. No real sign-in, live tunnel or upstream acceptance.
Browser uses a loopback fixture ingress, fixed canonical host and the hash-verified candidate client buffer; no production proxy was added.
Provider-health classification is separately verified by the established relay suite; the HTTP fixture counts only its explicit failure signals.
No host reboot, forced sleep or Docker daemon failure was induced.

revocation.design: No grant-cache delay. Each admission checks current grant under database locking; no new admission after successful revocation acknowledgement. Already admitted work may finish once.
revocation.historical_175_ms: Retained historical acceptance, not an SLA or comparison target.
